source_evidence: During the accumulation phase, you make either a lump sum payment or a series of payments to the insurance company.
answer: An indexed annuity has two phases. During the accumulation, or savings, phase, you pay the insurance company either once or through a series of payments. Those payments can be allocated to indexed investment options, and the insurer credits your account with a return based on the chosen option. During the annuity, or payout, phase, the insurer makes periodic payments to you; alternatively, you can choose to receive the contract value as one lump sum.
